findings: The primary specimen is identifiable as an adult Little Blue Heron: dark slaty-blue body, purple-maroon head and neck, yellow eye, two-toned blue-gray-and-black bill, olive legs, slender proportions, rounded folded wings, and short tail agree with the direct sources and adult reference photos.

The plate contains exactly one complete primary specimen with one head, one bill, two folded wings represented in the layered side view, two legs, and one tail. The detached wing and head are clearly isolated supplementary studies and do not appear attached to the primary bird.

Both depicted heads have long, straight, spear-shaped bills with coherent upper and lower mandibles traced from a common base to clean, non-reversed tips. Their proportions are mutually consistent and agree with the clearest attached side-profile references; the allowed direct sources do not identify unequal mandible projection as a species field mark.

The primary bird's eye, neck, body, wing, tail, leg, and foot colors and proportions are consistent with the adult references. The perched feet are stylized and partly occluded by the branch but remain anatomically plausible, with no extra or fused limbs.

The detached wing has a plausible rounded heron-wing outline and orderly covert, secondary, and primary feather groups. The detached head preserves the adult plumage pattern, yellow eye, and two-toned bill without malformed anatomy.
The common name, scientific name Egretta caerulea, and family Ardeidae are correct.

The printed measurements—length 56–74 cm (22.1–29.1 in), wingspan 100–105 cm (39.4–41.3 in), and weight 296–412 g (10.4–14.5 oz)—exactly match the Cornell identification page. Audubon independently supports the same length and an overlapping rounded wingspan and weight range.

Every visible habitat, behavior, and field-mark sentence is legible and complete, with no duplicated, omitted, substituted, or nonsensical words. The claims agree with the independently verified descriptions of wetland habitat, deliberate shallow-water foraging, diet, colonial nesting, tucked-neck flight, adult coloration, white juvenile plumage, calico immatures, bill coloration, yellow eyes, greenish legs, rounded wings, and short tail.

The body-length ruler is internally consistent: 56 cm (22.1 in) is at the bottom, 74 cm (29.1 in) is at the top, values increase upward, exactly four evenly spaced unlabeled interior ticks form five proportional segments, and the repeated body-length label agrees with both endpoints. “SCHEMATIC — NOT TO SCALE” clearly prevents interpreting it as the printed bird's physical scale.
The five palette swatches correspond in order to the stated slaty blue, purple-maroon, white, pale blue-gray, and olive-green field colors.
No place name, ZIP code, coordinates, map, or local-observation detail appears.
